implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: a fixed array plus two indices, head (producer-owned) and tail (consumer-owned), that wrap instead of shifting. Enqueue writes at head and advances it; dequeue reads at tail and advances it. Size the capacity to a power of two so the wrap is a mask (i + 1) & (size - 1) rather than a modulo. Disambiguate full from empty with the wasted-slot convention or an explicit count. In the single-producer single-consumer case, order the operations: the producer writes the item then release-stores the head; the consumer acquire-loads the head before reading the item. State the policy at capacity - overwrite oldest, drop newest, or signal - and, if data loss matters, keep sequence numbers so the consumer can detect an overrun. Pad the two indices onto separate cache lines when shared between cores.
idiom_name: fixed array with wrapping head/tail indices, power-of-two masking, and acquire/release ordering per side
pitfalls: Full vs empty ambiguity: head == tail means both unless one slot is wasted or a count is kept.
Missing the release store after writing the item: the consumer can read an unwritten slot. Invisible in functional tests.
Both indices on one cache line: the ping-pong makes the 'lock-free' ring slower than a mutex. Pad them apart.
Silently overwriting a stream the consumer treats as lossless - keep sequence numbers so the loss is detectable.
